questions.question: When driving a heavy vehicle, how can you avoid interfering with traffic?

options.text: Pass other vehicles while going uphill.
Ride the brakes while going downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match the speed of other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous material label does not fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to the package instead.
Make the label smaller so it fits on the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: A pre-trip vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
Is not required for trips under 100 miles.
Can only be done by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and wear. The correct tightness varies by vehicle, so check your vehicle's requirements.

questions.question: When visibility is low, like at dawn or dusk, what should you do to help other drivers see your vehicle?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will stop your turn signals from working.
Are safe if you only drive on highways.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds your axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers can be dangerous defects.

questions.question: A box containing liquid containers must display:

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials packages with liquid containers must have arrows marking which side should face up.

questions.question: If you see a large box in your lane ahead, you should:

options.text: Not worry because another vehicle will probably hit it first.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see objects in your lane. Even a cardboard box could contain items that damage your vehicle.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Always drive so you can stop completely within the area of road you can see ahead of you.

questions.question: Keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
questions.explanation: Keep enough space between your vehicle and others. This gives you room to stop without hitting someone if needed.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Get all wheels onto the shoulder.
Stop safely before getting back on the road, if you can.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before getting back on the road, if you can.
questions.explanation: If you must drive onto the shoulder, try to keep one set of wheels on the pavement for better control. Stop completely on the shoulder if possible. Then pull back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles like reflective triangles.

questions.question: What should a driver always do?

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Look ahead while driving to spot hazards early. Think about what you would do if a hazard becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to someone in the vehicle.
Children on the side of the road.
Construction workers on the side of the road.
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to others may not pay full attention to the road. Children may run into the road without looking. Be careful around construction workers. A person waiting for a bus on a bench is not a concern.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, turn on the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before you get in the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved convex mirrors. These mirrors let you see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When carrying hazardous materials, placards should be:

options.text: Put on all four sides of the vehicle.
Used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be displayed on all four sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: How much water does it take for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A lot, like a large puddle.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip with the road and slide on a layer of water. It does not take much water for this to happen.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always allowed. When carrying Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials, heaters are usually prohibited.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, like at dawn or dusk, how can you make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights to make your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams when driving near other vehicles.

questions.question: Brake pads should:

options.text: Not have any oil or grease on them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not have any oil or grease on them.
questions.explanation: Brake pads must be clean. They should not have any oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: If a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) but the tractor does not:

options.text: The truck should not be driven because both the tractor and trailer need ABS.
The truck should be driven more slowly than usual.
The tractor should not be used and a new one with ABS should be found.
The tractor and trailer can still be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor and trailer can still be used together.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on only the tractor or only the trailer gives extra braking control. You can still use them together.

questions.question: A cardboard box on the road:

options.text: Should be avoided by driving off the roadway.

questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box may look harmless but could contain something hard or heavy that damages your vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1 materials, the floor liner should be:
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner for Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight and the liner must be made from non-metal or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the roadway. If possible, avoid driving in fog.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items covering the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards. These include drivers with ice on windshields, drivers with items blocking windows, and drivers unfamiliar with rental trucks' limited rear visibility. A person simply driving a pick-up truck is not hazardous.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should not:

options.text: Cancel the turn signal after completing the turn.
Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is finished.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is finished.
questions.explanation: Signal well ahead of your turn or lane change. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change. Then turn off the signal so other drivers are not confused.

questions.question: Good drivers look ____ seconds ahead of their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This helps you react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: To get a HazMat endorsement, you must pass a background check from which agency?
questions.explanation: To get a new or renewed HazMat endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: If you are pulled over on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use the taillights to alert other motorists.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Set out items from the cab to warn motorists.

questions.explanation: If you must stop on the roadside, turn on your emergency flashers and place warning signals to alert other drivers.
